_note: Run: python3 bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/basic5-protocol.json (standard-library-only tests -- no torch/numpy venv needed). These prove tests/test_basic5_protocol.py is not vacuous: the protocol document (docs/BASIC5_PROTOCOL.md) is machinery, not just prose. Mutant 1 flips bin/extract-features.py's default saved representation to 'raw' while the document still declares 'l2', which must break the doc<->code agreement test -- the two cannot drift apart unnoticed. Mutant 2 removes the FAIR rule 'c' row from the document, which must break the 'every canonical rule id is documented' test -- a rule cannot silently drop out of the source of truth. The rule-table parser itself carries its own positive and negative controls (TestRuleParserControls), so a detector that decides what counts as a rule is proven both ways.
